Problem: The matrix for projecting onto a certain plane $P,$ which passes through the origin, is given by
\[\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5} \begin{pmatrix} \frac{13}{14} & -\frac{1}{7} & \frac{3}{14} \\ -\frac{1}{7} & \frac{5}{7} & \frac{3}{7} \\ \frac{3}{14} & \frac{3}{7} & \frac{5}{14} \end{pmatrix} \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1}.\]Find the normal vector of plane $P.$  Enter your answer in the form $\begin{pmatrix} a \\ b \\ c \end{pmatrix},$ where $a,$ $b,$ and $c$ are integers, $a > 0,$ and $\gcd(|a|,|b|,|c|) = 1.$

Solve step by step. End with: The answer is [your answer].

message.content:
The projection matrix onto plane \(P\) satisfies  
\[
P=I-\mathbf{n}\mathbf{n}^T
\]
for a unit normal vector \(\mathbf{n}\). Thus
\[
I-P=\mathbf{n}\mathbf{n}^T.
\]

Compute:
\[
I-P=
\begin{pmatrix}
1 & 0 & 0\\
0 & 1 & 0\\
0 & 0 & 1
\end{pmatrix}
-
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac{13}{14} & -\frac{1}{7} & \frac{3}{14} \\
-\frac{1}{7} & \frac{5}{7} & \frac{3}{7} \\
\frac{3}{14} & \frac{3}{7} & \frac{5}{14}
\end{pmatrix}
=
\frac1{14}
\begin{pmatrix}
1 & 2 & -3\\
2 & 4 & -6\\
-3 & -6 & 9
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

This equals
\[
\frac1{14}
\begin{pmatrix}
1\\2\\-3
\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}
1&2&-3
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

So a normal vector is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
1\\2\\-3
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

The answer is \(\begin{pmatrix}1\\2\\-3\end{pmatrix}\).
